input.strategy_title: AMD GPU (ROCm) enablement for serving and training
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Two strategic customers are standardizing on AMD Instinct accelerators and need
RHOAI to serve and train on ROCm. Upstream vLLM and PyTorch both publish ROCm
support, but the platform ships only CUDA runtime builds, and we have no
first-hand data on functional or performance parity for our supported model
set. Feature and performance validation requires physical AMD GPU hardware —
none exists in our CI fleet today — and upstream ROCm image cadence is
controlled by AMD and the upstream communities.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | A validation campaign on physical AMD Instinct hardware establishes functional and performance parity data for vLLM serving of the supported model set, producing the go/no-go scope for productization. |
| HLR-2 | P0 | A supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime is productized for the models the validation campaign clears. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | PyTorch training on ROCm is supported for single- and multi-GPU jobs admitted through Kueue, with amd.com/gpu quota handling. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation states supported AMD hardware, driver prerequisites, and the validated model list. |

## Affected Components

- KServe
- Serving Runtimes
- Training Operator
- Distributed Workloads

## Out of Scope

- Intel Gaudi or other non-AMD accelerator families
- AMD GPU sharing/partitioning support

## Open Questions

1. Hardware access: the validation campaign (HLR-1) needs dedicated AMD
   Instinct nodes — procurement or partner-lab access is unresolved.
2. Upstream ROCm build cadence: whether AMD's runtime image releases align
   with our release trains is outside our control.

# AMD Instinct validation campaign for vLLM ROCm serving

## Description

This epic resolves the strategy's central unknown: whether vLLM serving on AMD Instinct accelerators reaches functional and performance parity with the productized CUDA builds for our supported model set. It runs a validation campaign on physical AMD Instinct hardware and produces a per-model report with functional pass/fail results, performance measurements against the CUDA baseline, and a go/no-go recommendation that defines the productization scope. The platform currently ships only CUDA runtime builds and has no first-hand parity data, so this campaign is the gate for all serving productization work in this strategy.

## Scope

- Define the validation plan: enumerate the supported model set and the functional and performance parity criteria to be measured for each model.
- Obtain execution access to physical AMD Instinct GPU nodes (procurement or partner-lab access — see Risks).
- Serve every model in the supported model set with the upstream vLLM ROCm runtime on AMD Instinct hardware.
- Record functional results (correct inference behavior vs the CUDA baseline) and performance measurements (throughput and latency) per model.
- Produce a validation report with a per-model go/no-go recommendation and the resulting productization scope.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A validation plan exists that enumerates the supported model set and defines the functional and performance parity criteria measured for each model.
- Every model in the supported model set has been served with the vLLM ROCm runtime on physical AMD Instinct hardware and has a recorded functional pass/fail result against the CUDA baseline.
- Every model in the supported model set has recorded performance measurements (throughput and latency) on AMD Instinct hardware alongside comparable CUDA-baseline numbers.
- A validation report is published with a per-model go/no-go recommendation that defines the productization scope for the vLLM ROCm serving runtime.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): validation campaign on physical AMD Instinct hardware establishing functional and performance parity data for vLLM serving of the supported model set, producing the go/no-go scope for productization — fully covered by this epic.

## Risks and Notes

- **Hardware access is unresolved** (strategy open question): dedicated AMD Instinct nodes require procurement or partner-lab access. This is an externally-controlled availability precondition — the epic's deliverable is the validated report; securing access is effort within the epic, but the access being granted is not a condition the deliverable itself produces.
- **Upstream ROCm image cadence** is controlled by AMD and the upstream communities; the campaign consumes upstream ROCm builds and may need to re-run against newer images.
- The campaign also exercises KServe InferenceService deployment behavior on AMD GPU nodes; findings feed the serving runtime productization scope.

# Productize the vLLM ROCm serving runtime

## Description

This epic delivers a supported, productized vLLM serving runtime built for AMD Instinct accelerators (ROCm), covering the models the validation campaign clears. Today only CUDA (NVIDIA) builds of the vLLM runtime are productized; ROCm builds exist upstream but are neither shipped nor supported. This epic turns the cleared subset of the supported model set into a shipped, supported runtime for the platform.

## Scope

- Build and release a ROCm variant of the vLLM serving runtime image in the existing midstream vLLM repository and release pipeline, scoped to the models cleared by the validation campaign.
- Provide the ServingRuntime/ClusterServingRuntime definitions that expose the ROCm runtime variant for AMD GPU nodes.
- Verify KServe InferenceService deployment with the ROCm runtime (KServe itself requires no code change — it is validated as a passive component by the same team).
- Track upstream vLLM ROCm releases and pin to compatible upstream image versions per platform release (upstream cadence risk, see Risks).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A ROCm build of the vLLM serving runtime is produced and released through the platform release pipeline, scoped to the models cleared by the validation campaign.
- The ROCm runtime image builds green in the Konflux build pipeline (the build-pipeline onboarding for this image runs in parallel with this epic; its coupling is enforced by this acceptance criterion, not by a dependency between the two work items).
- Every model cleared by the validation campaign deploys and serves correctly via a KServe InferenceService using the ROCm runtime on AMD GPU nodes.
- The runtime ships with a support statement identifying the cleared model set and the AMD hardware it is validated on.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0): a supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime productized for the models the validation campaign clears — covered by this epic together with the Konflux build-pipeline work for the ROCm image (a work-product-type split: runtime productization vs. build-pipeline onboarding).

## Risks and Notes

- **Upstream ROCm build cadence** (strategy open question): whether AMD's runtime image releases align with our release trains is outside our control. If cadence misaligns, the runtime pins to or rebuilds from the nearest compatible upstream release — fix-and-retry, not a structural change.
- The scope of this epic is rewritten (not merely trimmed) by the validation campaign outcome: the cleared model set defines what is productized and what the support statement covers.

# Konflux build pipeline for the vLLM ROCm runtime image

## Description

This epic onboards the vLLM ROCm container image build into Konflux, the platform's build pipeline, so the ROCm runtime variant is built, scanned, and attested with the same release rigor as the existing CUDA runtime images. The vLLM midstream repository is already Konflux-onboarded for its CUDA images; this epic adds the pipeline configuration for the new ROCm image variant.

## Scope

- Add Konflux build-pipeline configuration for the vLLM ROCm container image in the existing midstream vLLM repository.
- Wire the image build, including its base-image and dependency inputs, into the pipeline's build and release tasks.
- Ensure the pipeline produces the image with the required attestations so it can ship as a supported runtime artifact.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A Konflux build pipeline configuration exists for the vLLM ROCm container image in the midstream vLLM repository.
- The pipeline produces a green build of the ROCm image, including the required signed attestations for release.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0): a supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime productized for the cleared models — this epic provides the build-pipeline half of that productization (work-product-type split from the runtime productization work; the two run in parallel by rule, coupled only through the runtime epic's build-pipeline-green acceptance criterion).

## Risks and Notes

- The ROCm image's base layers come from AMD's published ROCm images; upstream base-image cadence may require pipeline input updates (fix-and-retry, not a structural change).

# PyTorch ROCm training enablement for PyTorchJob workloads

## Description

This epic enables PyTorch training on AMD Instinct accelerators (ROCm) for workloads run through the platform's Training Operator: single-GPU and multi-GPU PyTorchJob jobs execute on AMD GPU nodes using ROCm builds of PyTorch. Today accelerated training in the platform is NVIDIA-only; this epic extends the supported training paths to AMD hardware.

## Scope

- Enable PyTorchJob workloads to run with ROCm builds of PyTorch on AMD GPU nodes, for both single-GPU and multi-GPU (multi-node) job topologies.
- Provide/validate the training images and runtime prerequisites for ROCm jobs admitted through Kueue queueing.
- Verify end-to-end admission and completion of ROCm training jobs through Kueue with amd.com/gpu quota (requires coordination with the Kueue amd.com/gpu quota handling work in this strategy — a coordination point, not a dependency).

## Acceptance Criteria

- PyTorchJob workloads using ROCm run to completion on AMD GPU nodes for both single-GPU and multi-GPU job topologies.
- Multi-GPU ROCm PyTorchJobs are admitted through Kueue queueing with amd.com/gpu quota accounted, and complete successfully end to end.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P1): PyTorch training on ROCm supported for single- and multi-GPU jobs admitted through Kueue, with amd.com/gpu quota handling — this epic covers the training-operator side; the Kueue quota side is covered by the Distributed Workloads (Kueue) epic for the same HLR.

## Risks and Notes

- **Upstream ROCm build cadence** (strategy open question): PyTorch ROCm image releases are controlled by AMD and upstream communities; misalignment with release trains is handled by pinning or rebuilding.
- Validation of training on physical AMD Instinct hardware depends on the same unresolved hardware-access precondition noted in the strategy (procurement or partner-lab access) — a schedule risk, not a structural one.

# Kueue quota handling for amd.com/gpu resources

## Description

This epic extends the platform's queueing layer (Kueue) so that AMD GPU resources (amd.com/gpu) are handled correctly in quota accounting and workload admission: training workloads requesting AMD GPUs are admitted against amd.com/gpu quota with the same all-or-nothing gang semantics as existing accelerated workloads. Today quota handling and GPU resource discovery in the platform are oriented to NVIDIA GPUs.

## Scope

- Support amd.com/gpu as a quota-accounted resource in the Kueue ClusterQueue/LocalQueue quota model.
- Ensure single- and multi-GPU workloads requesting amd.com/gpu are admitted only when their full GPU request can be satisfied (all-or-nothing admission for gang-scheduled jobs).
- Verify quota enforcement for AMD GPU workloads end to end together with the PyTorch ROCm training enablement in this strategy (coordination point, not a dependency).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Workloads requesting amd.com/gpu are admitted against configured quota when available, and queued or denied when the quota is exhausted, with quota accounting matching the configured amd.com/gpu limits.
- Multi-GPU workloads requesting amd.com/gpu are admitted only when the full GPU request can be satisfied (all-or-nothing gang admission).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P1): PyTorch training on ROCm supported for single- and multi-GPU jobs admitted through Kueue, with amd.com/gpu quota handling — this epic covers the Kueue quota-handling side; the Training Operator side is covered by the PyTorch ROCm training epic for the same HLR.

## Risks and Notes

- End-to-end verification requires AMD GPU nodes in a test cluster — subject to the strategy's unresolved hardware-access precondition (schedule risk, not a structural one).

# Documentation for AMD GPU (ROCm) enablement

## Description

This epic documents the AMD GPU (ROCm) enablement delivered by this strategy: the supported AMD Instinct hardware, GPU driver prerequisites, and the validated model list for vLLM ROCm serving, plus the supported PyTorch training paths on ROCm with amd.com/gpu quota configuration. Documentation runs last so it describes what was actually built and validated.

## Scope

Content outline (topics to author within the documentation set):

- Supported AMD Instinct hardware for RHOAI serving and training.
- GPU driver and ROCm runtime prerequisites for AMD GPU nodes.
- The validated model list for the vLLM ROCm serving runtime, as cleared by the validation campaign.
- Configuring vLLM ROCm serving on AMD GPU nodes (runtime selection via ServingRuntime).
- Running PyTorch training on ROCm: single- and multi-GPU PyTorchJob jobs admitted through Kueue.
- Configuring amd.com/gpu quota in the Kueue ClusterQueue/LocalQueue quota model.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Documentation states the supported AMD Instinct hardware and the GPU driver prerequisites for serving and training.
- Documentation lists the validated model set for the vLLM ROCm serving runtime, matching the models cleared by the validation campaign.
- Documentation covers PyTorch training on ROCm through Kueue, including amd.com/gpu quota configuration guidance.
- All documented claims are technically reviewed against the shipped implementation (serving runtime, training enablement, and quota handling as delivered).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P2): documentation states supported AMD hardware, driver prerequisites, and the validated model list — fully covered by this epic. This epic's priority (P1) is derived from the strategy's overall priority (Major) per the docs-authoring priority rule, not from HLR-4's P2 label.
